name: EMPOWUR
question: Does vibegron 75 mg once daily reduce daily micturitions and urge incontinence episodes over 12 weeks compared with placebo in adults with overactive bladder?

arms.label: tolterodine extended release 4 mg once daily

design.population: Adults with overactive bladder for at least 3 months, 85.2% women, 42.9% aged 65 or older, including up to 25% without urge incontinence.
design.description: International, double-blind, placebo- and active-controlled randomized trial
design.locator: Arms and 5:5:4 ratio: Abstract; arm counts: Frankel 2021 Results, Patients, and ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03492281 participant flow (Fig. 1 of the paper is an image); population: Staskin 2020 Results, Study Participants, and Table 1

verdictNote: Both co-primary endpoints met versus placebo; vibegron was not formally compared with the tolterodine reference arm.
takeaway: In adults with overactive bladder, vibegron 75 mg daily reduced daily micturitions (1.8 versus 1.3 fewer) and, with urge incontinence, its episodes (2.0 versus 1.4 fewer) more than placebo over 12 weeks; tolterodine extended release, the active reference, gave 1.6 and 1.8.

reports.label: 12-week randomized report
reports.citation: Staskin D, Frankel J, Varano S, et al. International phase III, randomized, double-blind, placebo and active controlled study to evaluate the safety and efficacy of vibegron in patients with symptoms of overactive bladder: EMPOWUR. *J Urol.* 2020;204(2):316-324. doi:10.1097/JU.0000000000000807
reports.followUpLocator: Results, Study Participants (12-week treatment, 4-week follow-up safety evaluation)

results.measure: Co-primary: least-squares mean change from baseline to week 12 in average daily micturitions (all patients); difference is vibegron minus placebo (episodes per day); tested at two-sided alpha 0.05 in a predefined hierarchy
results.locator: Results, Co-primary Efficacy End Points; Fig. 2A; Statistical Analyses
results.note: Patients with week-12 data: 492 vibegron, 475 placebo, 378 tolterodine (full analysis set 526, 520 and 417). Tolterodine versus placebo, supportive with nominal P: difference −0.3 (95% CI −0.6 to 0.1; P=0.0988). Vibegron was not compared with tolterodine. Difference versus placebo was significant from week 2 (prespecified exploratory) and at all later time points. Sample size gave about 98% power for a 0.60 difference (SD 2.20).

results.measure: Co-primary: least-squares mean change from baseline to week 12 in average daily urge incontinence episodes in OAB wet patients; difference is vibegron minus placebo (episodes per day); tested after micturitions in the hierarchy
results.locator: Results, Co-primary Efficacy End Points; Fig. 2B; Statistical Analyses
results.note: Patients with week-12 data: 383 vibegron, 372 placebo, 286 tolterodine (full analysis set for incontinence 403, 405 and 319; mean baseline 3.5 episodes/day). Tolterodine versus placebo (supportive): difference −0.4 (95% CI −0.7 to −0.1; P=0.0123). Difference versus placebo was significant from week 2. Sample size gave about 98% power for a 0.51 difference (SD 1.68).

results.measure: Least-squares mean change from baseline to week 12 in average daily urgency episodes; difference is vibegron minus placebo (episodes per day); first key secondary endpoint in the hierarchy
results.locator: Results, Key Secondary Efficacy End Points; Fig. 3A
results.note: Patients with week-12 data: 492 vibegron, 475 placebo, 378 tolterodine; mean baseline 8.1 urgency episodes/day. Tolterodine versus placebo (supportive): difference −0.4 (95% CI −0.9 to 0.0; P=0.0648). Significant versus placebo from week 2.

results.measure: Least-squares mean change from baseline to week 12 in average volume voided per micturition; difference is vibegron minus placebo (mL)
results.locator: Results, Key Secondary Efficacy End Points; Fig. 3B
results.note: Patients with week-12 data: 490 vibegron, 478 placebo, 375 tolterodine; mean baseline 150.5 mL. Tolterodine versus placebo (supportive): difference 13.3 mL (95% CI 5.9 to 20.7; P<0.001). Significant versus placebo from week 2.

results.measure: OAB wet patients with at least 75% reduction from baseline in average daily urge incontinence episodes at week 12
results.locator: Results, Key Secondary Efficacy End Points; Fig. 3C
results.note: Full analysis set for incontinence: 403 vibegron, 405 placebo, 319 tolterodine; Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel risk difference stratified by sex, multiple imputation for missing data. The paper prints unadjusted percentages; the ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03492281 results give sex-adjusted percentages 49.3%, 32.8% and 42.2% and a difference of 16.5 points (95% CI 9.7 to 23.4). Significant versus placebo from week 2.

results.measure: OAB wet patients with 100% reduction in daily urge incontinence episodes at week 12, sex-adjusted percentage; difference in percentage points
results.locator: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03492281 results, OAB-wet 100% UUI reduction at week 12 (not reported in the paper's text)
results.note: Denominators 403, 405 and 319; unadjusted percentages 28.8%, 22.5% and 26.6%.

harms.label: Any adverse event
harms.note: Safety analysis set: all patients who received at least one dose of double-blind medication.

harms.label: Adverse event of clinical interest
harms.note: Protocol-defined: major cardiac or cerebrovascular events, new or worsened hypertension, increased blood pressure, orthostatic hypotension, cystitis or urinary tract infection, and liver enzyme elevations leading to interruption or discontinuation.

harms.label: Serious adverse events
harms.note: One death, in the tolterodine arm (stroke, urinary tract infection and sepsis; unrelated to study drug per investigator and sponsor). Two vibegron events (pneumonia and noncardiac chest pain) were judged possibly or probably related by the investigator but not the sponsor.

harms.label: Discontinuation for adverse events
harms.note: Causes in more than one patient: headache 6 (3 vibegron, 1 placebo, 2 tolterodine), dry mouth 4 (all tolterodine), hypertension 3 (1 vibegron, 2 placebo), diarrhea 2 (both tolterodine).

harms.label: Hypertension
harms.note: Hypertension was a predefined adverse event of interest. No clinically relevant difference in posttreatment blood pressure between hypertensive and nonhypertensive patients at baseline.

harms.label: Headache
harms.note: With nasopharyngitis (15, 9 and 11 patients; 2.8%, 1.7% and 2.6%), diarrhea (12, 6 and 9; 2.2%, 1.1% and 2.1%) and nausea (12, 6 and 5; 2.2%, 1.1% and 1.2%), the events above 2.0% on vibegron and more frequent than placebo.

delivery.label: Randomization and treatment
delivery.value: 5:5:4 to vibegron 75 mg, placebo or tolterodine extended release 4 mg, each taken orally once daily each morning for 12 weeks; stratified by sex and wet versus dry OAB; double-dummy (placebo group received both matching placebos)

delivery.label: Study periods
delivery.value: 1- to 5-week screening, 28-day washout, 2-week single-blind placebo run-in, 12-week double-blind treatment, 4-week follow-up safety evaluation; 7-day voiding diaries at baseline and weeks 2, 4, 8 and 12, with a measured-volume diary on one of the 7 days

delivery.label: Run-in and screening
delivery.value: 3,149 screened; 1,518 randomized after a 2-week single-blind placebo run-in

delivery.label: Enrollment and sites
delivery.value: 1,518 randomized at 199 sites beginning March 26, 2018; last patient completed 12 weeks on January 7, 2019; 89.6% of the full analysis set enrolled in the United States (1,311/1,463)

delivery.label: Completion
delivery.locator: Results, Study Participants (90.4%); ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03492281 results, participant flow (arm counts)

delivery.label: Analysis sets
delivery.value: Full analysis set 1,463 (96.4%): 526 vibegron, 520 placebo, 417 tolterodine; full analysis set for incontinence (OAB wet) 1,127: 403, 405 and 319

delivery.label: Sample size
delivery.value: Planned about 500 vibegron, 500 placebo and 400 tolterodine; about 98% power at two-sided 0.05 for a 0.60 difference in micturitions (SD 2.20) and a 0.51 difference in urge incontinence episodes (SD 1.68)

delivery.label: Baseline (full analysis set)
delivery.value: Mean 11.5 micturitions, 8.1 urgency episodes and 150.5 mL per micturition per day; mean 3.5 urge incontinence episodes per day in the incontinence set; 85.2% women; 42.9% aged 65 or older; OAB wet 76.5% to 77.9% by arm

delivery.label: Statistical handling
delivery.value: Mixed model for repeated measures; responders by Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel risk difference stratified by sex and OAB category; multiple imputation for missing data; co-primary and key secondary endpoints in a predefined hierarchy; vibegron versus placebo was the formal comparison and all other comparisons were supportive with nominal P values and no multiplicity adjustment
